subject: POC trial: Success criteria & KPIs (latency, throughput, cost, quality) - next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Walker <ewalker@atlas-payments.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery call recap + proposed POC success criteria

Hi Ethan / team 
 great to meet earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Call highlights:
- Primary use: real-time payments fraud scoring & risk text enrichment for support flows.
- Expected peak concurrent requests: ~350 QPS (but starting small).
- Data sensitivity: PII present in certain fields; must meet Atlas security requirements (no training, optional VPC).
- Key risks: latency in support flows, and cost at scale.

Proposed POC goal (success criteria):
1) Latency: p95 generation latency <= 300ms for 512-token context in our non-blocking inference path.
2) Throughput: sustain 200 QPS with 95% successful responses (no OOM/failures) during a controlled ramp.
3) Cost: model + infra cost per 1k tokens <= $5 (i.e., cost/token <= $0.005) under POC config.
4) Quality: for the evaluation prompt set (sample attached), automated pass rate >= 90% on key intents; no critical hallucinations on payment/account queries.

POC plan (high-level):
- Week 0: Kickoff, environment access, data checklist & security review.
- Week 1: Baseline runs (latency + throughput) with synthetic traffic, collect logs.
- Week 2: Quality eval + prompt tuning using provided sample prompts.
- Week 3: Cost/perf tuning (quantization, batching), re-run benchmarks.
- Week 4: Decision & handoff (go/no-go + recommendation).

Ownership:
- Jordan Blake (me): overall POC lead, cadence & reporting.
- Marissa Cole: quality and prompt evaluation (owner of rubric & scoring).
- Dev Patel: infra integration, sampling keys & environment setup.
- Atlas: provide sample data, key security contact, and access to test environment.

Attachments: redwood_poc_mopack.pdf (PoC plan + test scripts), poc_timelines.xlsx (detailed timeline).

Requested next steps (can we confirm by EOD tomorrow?):
- Atlas confirms data access and legal contact for a brief security review.
- Agree on kickoff window next week (we have open slots Tue/Wed 9–11 PT).
- Any additional success metric you want added?

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Ethan Walker <ewalker@atlas-payments.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery call recap + proposed POC success criteria

Jordan — thanks for the fast recap and the attachments. A few quick notes from our side:

1) The latency targets look reasonable but our support flows are extremely latency-sensitive during peak hours. Can you confirm p50 and p95 targets and whether model warm-start / KV cache is included in the benchmark?
2) Cost metric is critical — can you show example cost math for your recommended model variants (e.g., 3B vs 13B quantized)?
3) Security: we need confirmation that no customer data will be used to continue training and that logs can be exported to our S3 with 90-day retention. Also want to schedule a short call with our security team (Wed or Thu).

We can do kickoff Wed 9:30 PT.


Ethan Walker
Head of Product (Payments)
Atlas Payments

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Walker <ewalker@atlas-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery call recap + proposed POC success criteria — plan + answers

Ethan — thanks, answers below and updated plan attached.

Answers / clarifications:
- Latency: we'll measure p50/p95/p99. Baseline target: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 300ms for 512-token generation on the recommended 13B optimized variant with KV cache enabled. Benchmarks will explicitly note warm vs cold cache.
- Cost math: included in redwood_poc_mopack.pdf (section 3) — short version: 13B quantized + batching expected cost ~= $3.80 per 1k tokens under the proposed batching and cache settings; 3B variant is cheaper but shows lower quality on our sample. We'll run both variants during POC.
- Security: confirmed — no customer data used for training. We can stream logs to your S3 (90-day retention) or provide a secure link; we'll also offer a VPC/private deployment option if you need stronger isolation.

Updated evaluation plan (concrete tests):
1) Latency test: controlled generator that runs 1k samples across 512-token contexts; run with cold start and warm cache. Collect p50/p95/p99 and failure rates.
2) Throughput ramp: synthetic traffic ramp from 10 QPS -> 200 QPS over 2 hours and observe errors/OOMs.
3) Cost calc: run representative workload simulation (tokens per request distribution attached) and output cost per 1k tokens for each model/config.
4) Quality eval: Marissa to run rubric-based scoring on a 100-sample prompt set (attached). Pass threshold: >= 90% automated pass rate + no critical hallucinations.

Decision criteria (end of week 4):
- Go: meets latency and throughput thresholds, cost within ±15% of target, and quality above threshold.
- No-go: any single critical failure (security/PII leak or repeated OOMs) or quality below 80%.

Proposed timeline (kickoff Wed 9:30 PT):
- Wed (kickoff): environment & access + security sync with Atlas sec team.
- Fri: baseline latency runs complete.
- Next Tue: quality eval results.
- Next Thu: cost/perf tuning run and final decision.

Action items assigned:
- Jordan: schedule kickoff & send calendar invite (done).
- Marissa: prepare prompt set & rubric (deliverable Tue).
- Dev: provision test environment and S3 integration (deliverable Wed EOD).
- Atlas: security contact + sample data (deliverable Wed morning).

Attachments: redwood_poc_mopack.pdf, poc_timelines.xlsx.

If that looks good I'll send the kickoff invite and a short runbook for the tests.

Thanks — Jordan

[Attachment: redwood_poc_mopack.pdf (pdf, 580KB) — PoC plan, test scripts, cost math]
[Attachment: poc_timelines.xlsx (xlsx) — week-by-week timeline]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery call recap + proposed POC success criteria — Marissa owns quality eval

Quick note — I will own the quality evaluation and deliver the 100-sample prompt set + scoring rubric by Tue morning as discussed.

I'll include examples that target the three most common failure modes we saw on the call: intent misclassification, hallucination on payment details, and unsafe content filtering. I'll also add a small user-acceptance slice that EM can sanity-check.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
